_note: ADDITIVE. contract/contract.json is under blind test by nxb-009 and was NOT modified. H2 needs a receipt whose hop is 'H2', and contract.json froze receipt.hop to enum ['H1']. That is a contract defect found by building: a closed enum in a v1 schema blocks the v2 that was always planned. When nxb-009 reports, merge this file and widen the enum.

h2_receipt.doc: Emitted by the broker when a runtime acknowledges receipt of work. For Codex this is thread.started on stdout. Emitted BEFORE any judgement about whether the work will succeed.

parent_receipt_id.doc: The H1 receipt this spawn descends from. Provenance chain, not provenance proof.

runtime_ref.doc: The runtime's OWN identifier for the work. Codex: thread_id UUID. Never a name. MUST be non-empty: a blank ref names nothing, and C14 showed it flowing through validation into a forged liveness proof.

pinned_model.doc: R-030. What the broker asked for. NOT what ran; that is H3's problem.

runtime_ref.doc: On an already_spawned refusal, the id of the child that DID run. The broker holds it and used to say nothing, so the work was unreachable.

evidence_path.doc: On an already_spawned refusal, the transcript that child wrote, if the runtime's locator resolves it.

items.rule: stdin MUST be /dev/null. Measured: with stdin open, codex exec emits zero bytes and never exits.
items.enforced_by: The spawn path attaches an empty, already-closed standard input to the child, so a runtime that blocks reading stdin cannot stall the spawn.

items.rule: No start signal within start_timeout means kill the child. The wait MUST be non-blocking: a timeout checked only between blocking reads cannot fire against a child that emits nothing.
items.enforced_by: The wait for a start signal is non-blocking: it observes the child's streams in a way that lets the timeout fire while every stream is silent, rather than only between completed reads.

items.rule: A broker may kill ONLY processes it holds a direct handle to, NEVER by command-line pattern. Pattern killing is cross-tenant destructive on a multi-agent machine and silent.
items.enforced_by: Termination targets only a process handle the broker itself holds. No path anywhere selects processes by command-line pattern.

items.rule: Exit code is NOT a failure signal for a spawn that never started. Measured: a child SIGINTed for missing its start signal exits 0.
items.enforced_by: A spawn's success is determined from its start signal and its declared output artifact. No path treats the child's exit code alone as evidence that the spawn started.

items.rule: The -o file's ABSENCE is a reliable failure signal; its PRESENCE is not a success signal.
items.enforced_by: The drain result reports the presence of the output artifact as a fact separate from success, and no path treats presence as success.

items.rule: One H2 receipt per H1 receipt. A second spawn attempt is refused, not silently deduplicated.
items.enforced_by: Each H2 spawn is keyed in the durable record on the H1 receipt it descends from, so a second spawn for the same parent receipt is refused rather than silently deduplicated.

items.rule: A refusal that the broker can only reach BECAUSE a spawn row exists MUST expose that row's runtime identifier. Refusing while holding direct evidence a child ran, and saying nothing about it, makes the work unreachable rather than absent.

measurements._source: nxb-010, this Mac, 2026-08-28, codex-cli 0.150.1, -m gpt-5.6-luna -s read-only, trivial prompt
measurements.verdict: A-023 was 30 seconds against an observed warm max of 0.167s and a cold 0.685s: 44x to 320x too generous. An over-long start timeout is not free: it is exactly how long a hung spawn holds a slot before the trap is detected.

_removed_refusal_terms.runtime_has_no_spawn: Never emitted. No code path refuses a runtime for lacking a spawn primitive. Removed under the vocabulary rule in contract.json rather than left as a term a consumer could match on and never see. [nxb-042]

_vocabulary_note: Published because they are emitted, under contract.json's _vocabulary_rule. `malformed_start_signal` is the one worth naming: a start signal that ARRIVED but carried no id is not a timeout, and reporting it as one sends the operator to the clock instead of to the runtime. It was emitted and unpublished for the whole life of this contract. [nxb-042]
